title: Production Policy
description: The single authoritative, versioned source for workflow limits, per-dimension gate thresholds, candidate policy, extraction thresholds, context-tail budgets and the issue-override matrix (ADR-0041, ADR-0042). One shipped starting version per quality tier; projects pin a version at job start. All numbers are starting values with calibration status (ADR-0029).

content_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON without this field

per_span_attempts.description: Attempts on one span before escalating scope

smoke_after_patches.description: Cumulative patches after which both judges re-run on the whole chapter

regression_tolerance_points.description: Max allowed per-dimension score drop between versions

ladder.description: ADR-0087 (STEP 3): the escalation ladder. A round whose open blocking/major findings include a kind in scene_rewrite_kinds (kinds the per-kind fix rates show patches rarely repair) drafts the scene holding them again from its scene plan instead of patching — the scene holding most of their spans, or for unquoted findings the scene furthest below its planned talk — at most max_scene_rewrites times per chapter; the rewrite is evaluated and regression-checked like a patch.

candidates_per_cluster.description: ADR-0087 (STEP 3): patches drafted per cluster of a multi-patch round; the one that brings the fewest new lint pattern hits (번역투 markers, AI stock phrases, calques) into its span is kept before any judge runs, the first on a tie. Absent or 1: one patch per cluster, as before.

on_regression.description: ADR-0064. stop (the default when absent): a patch that fails the ADR-0014 regression check stops the chapter as PATCH_REGRESSED. discard_and_continue: the patched version is quarantined, the chapter returns to the version before the patch and its scorecard, and the next round may revise again within the round limit

rounds_by_language.description: ADR-0064: revision rounds per manuscript language, replacing max_rounds for that language. Absent: English takes one representative round and Korean up to max_rounds (ADR-0056)

polish_pass.description: ADR-0073 (K1): after a Korean chapter passes its gates, one editor round on the Korean lint's 번역투, sentence-ending, dialogue-share and paragraph findings; the polished version is kept only if it still passes and the lint finds fewer of them, else it is quarantined (polish_rejected). Absent or false: no polish round

regression_baseline.description: ADR-0078 (V-1): what a patch's regression protections are measured against. absolute (the default when absent): every protected section must pass and no translation-like, register or westernization major may remain on the revised version, whatever the parent carried. parent: a protected section fails only when it passed on the parent and fails on the revision, and a kind guard fails only when the revision carries more open blocking/major issues of those kinds than the parent. The targeted-improvement, tolerance, dropped-dimension and new-issue-kind checks are the same in both.

convergence.description: ADR-0084 (V2, live defect G3-1): how revision rounds converge on a gate that allows no open major. rejudge_open_majors: after every patch, each evaluator whose findings on the parent include an open blocking or major issue re-runs on the new text, instead of carrying the finding forward. prefer_failing_dimension: a round targets a dimension whose gate failed whenever one has open blocking or major issues, so a passing dimension cannot take every round. Absent: carried findings and the most-issues dimension choice, as before.

span_attribution.description: ADR-0086 (V2, live defect G5-3b/c): a blocking or major finding on a patched version counts as introduced by the patch only when its quote lies in a paragraph the patch changed (or it quotes nothing and its evaluator re-ran on changed text); a finding on unchanged text is judge variance on text both versions share, so it stays open on the revision without failing the regression check. Absent or false: any new blocking/major issue kind fails the check (ADR-0014).

threshold_protection.description: ADR-0086 (G5-3a): a protected gated dimension counts as regressed only when the revision leaves it below its gate threshold and it fell by more than regression_tolerance_points. Absent or false: any fall beyond the tolerance regresses, even far above the threshold.

round_scope.description: ADR-0086 (G5-3d): dimension (the default when absent) patches one dimension's findings per round; all_open patches every open blocking and major finding of any dimension — continuity, knowledge, repetition included — in one round, clustered by span, and the regression check measures the union.

score_targets.description: ADR-0086 (G5-3e): a gated dimension that fails by score with no open blocking or major finding gets its judge's weakest passages as minor targets for the round, and its evaluator re-runs after every patch. Absent or false: a score-only failure is never targeted.

confirm_full.description: ADR-0086: a version that becomes approvable after a targeted re-evaluation is re-evaluated by every evaluator before approval; it is approved only if the full scorecard passes too. Absent or false: the targeted scorecard decides.

multi_patch.description: ADR-0077 (V1): a revision round asks the reviser for one patch per cluster of the targeted issues' spans (issues within merge_gap_chars of each other share a cluster; at most max_patches clusters, never more than max_patches_per_round) instead of one patch over the union of every span, and applies the usable patches together as one revision. A patch that cannot be anchored or validated is recorded and dropped; the round fails only when none is usable. Absent: one patch over the union of the targeted spans.

evaluation.description: Evaluation orchestration (ADR-0060). A policy without this block keeps the ADR-0056 behaviour: evaluators run one after another, only the seven core evaluators run, a gated dimension reads the judge's own 0-100 judge_score and every evaluator re-runs after a patch.

max_parallel_evaluators.description: Model evaluators of one manuscript version that may be in flight at once; results are assembled in a fixed order whatever the completion order

optional_evaluators.description: Evaluators beyond the core seven that run for every version; each writes its own scorecard section and gates through its blocking/major issues

score_model.description: judge_score: a gated dimension reads the judge's 0-100 number. rubric_subscores: the dimension score is judge_weight x the judge's 1-5 rubric sub-scores mapped to 0-100, plus (1 - judge_weight) x the dimension's deterministic composite

reevaluation.description: targeted: after a patch the deterministic checks and the targeted dimension's evaluator re-run, continuity and knowledge re-run when the patch changed claims, and every other evaluator re-runs only when one of its carried findings no longer anchors or revision.smoke_after_patches patches have accumulated since its last run

lint_penalty_points.description: Points a deterministic finding takes off its dimension's lint composite (starting at 100, floored at 0) under rubric_subscores

ledger_checks.description: ADR-0063: compare each draft with the state ledgers (countdowns against the story clock, the status-window format, registered address terms against the expected 말높이 (존댓말/반말)). Absent or false: no ledger check runs.

pov_secrets_reader_visible.description: ADR-0074 (live defect A-3): the chapter's POV character's own secrets are the narrator's knowledge and so the reader's; the knowledge-leak checker's reader-secret list leaves them out. In a regression serial the regressor's own return is the premise, not a leak. Absent or false: every unrevealed secret is listed.

length_in_structure.description: ADR-0081: the chapter length finding (LEN-01) counts against the structure dimension's deterministic composite, so a judge cannot rate the structure of a chapter far off its length target as if it were complete. Absent or false: length gates only through its own major finding, as before.

corpus_copy.description: ADR-0082 (C0.4): every evaluated version (draft, patch, polish) is checked against the operator corpus in the permanent database; a span sharing at least min_chars consecutive Hangul syllables, letters or digits with it (spaces and punctuation ignored) is a blocking corpus_copy finding. Absent: no corpus check.

judge_calibration.description: ADR-0081 (same-model judging): a judge's rubric score for a gated dimension may not exceed the dimension's deterministic composite by more than max_gap_points; above that it is capped there (never raised) and the cap is recorded on the scorecard section. Absent: rubric scores are used as the judge gave them.

drafting.description: Deterministic handling of scene drafts before assembly (ADR-0081).

paragraph_per_line.description: Every line break of a prose draft becomes a paragraph break (one paragraph per line, as serial platforms render it); words are untouched. Counted as the paragraph_per_line normalizer. Absent or false: drafts keep the model's own line layout.

reader_secrets_in_plan.description: ADR-0084 (U1, live defects A-4, G3-3): each scene plan the writer reads ends with the secrets the reader must not learn yet — the same list the knowledge-leak checker judges against (reveal chapter later than this one; under evaluation.pov_secrets_reader_visible the POV character's own secrets are left out). Absent or false: the writer sees only the contract's knowledge guards, as before.

planning.description: Pre-draft planning checks (ADR-0063). A policy without this block drafts every scene plan unchecked, as before.

plan_check.description: Check the contract and scene plans against the state ledgers, first meetings and the story clock before drafting. A blocking finding (an on-page character the ledger records as dead, story time running backwards) stops the chapter as PLAN_INCONSISTENT before any draft is written; other findings are recorded with the plan.

scene_plan_format.description: How a scene plan reaches a Korean writer (ADR-0068). 'json' (the same as absent) passes the plan object as JSON; 'labelled' renders it as labelled Korean text with names resolved from the registry. English writers always receive JSON.

design_batches.description: Generate the bible's cast in three checkpointed batches — protagonist, core cast, supporting cast — instead of one large character_designer call (ADR-0072). Each batch is its own checkpoint, so a rerun resumes after the last completed batch; later batches receive the names already designed and add the protagonist's registers toward the new characters. Absent or false: one call, as before.

rhythm_directives.description: Serial-rhythm directives for the chapter planner (ADR-0073): from the accepted contracts, a chapter is told to carry a 사이다 beat when the last two had none (사이다 within three 화; at most two 고구마 chapters in a row), the first 25 화 carry the funnel's denser cadence, and the 절단 must change the situation. The directives join the planner's hard constraints and a plan check records each (PLAN-RHYTHM-01..03). Absent or false: no directive.

reveal_schedule.description: ADR-0086 (U1, live defect G5-1): every bible secret gets a reader date (the first-person narrator's own secrets from 화 1; others at their reveal chapter, or reader_reveal_chapter when set), a date for the other characters and a knowledge layer (current, prior-life memory, source-work knowledge). The chapter planner, the writer and the knowledge-leak checker read one schedule; the contract lists the chapter's hidden secrets as reader_guards; a contract that reveals a hidden secret is repaired (PLAN-REVEAL-01). Absent: the ADR-0084 reader-secret list only.

hint_budget.description: Oblique hints per hidden secret per 화 the planner and writer are allowed.

plan_critic.description: ADR-0086 (U7, U8): before any drafting call the contract and scene plans are checked deterministically for self-consistency (participants, the final scene ending on the hook, dialogue beats with a partner, length) and by a plan_critic call (reveal safety, repeated exposition, character state against the schedule, the operator's structure targets). Blocking or major findings send the scene plan back to the scene planner with the findings, at most max_repairs times; the findings are recorded with the plan.

cut_design.description: ADR-0086 (U5, live defect G5-5): the final scene ends on the contract's hook — its last beat is the cut and the writer is told to stop there with no line after it; a draft whose last paragraph reads as a summary or reflection is re-drafted from its last scene once (kept when the ending lint passes).

time_frames.description: ADR-0086 (U3, live defect G5-6): bible secrets and character states that become true later carry the 화 they become true (true_from_chapter); packs and checkers read only what is true at the chapter being written, later states marked as planned.

dialogue_floor.description: ADR-0084 (U6, live defect G3-2): the scene plan carries enough talk. A scene whose planned dialogue share is below chapter_min is raised to it before drafting (the writer reads the target), and when partner_required and no scene puts anyone beside its POV character on stage, the longest scene gets the contract's first on-page participant who is not the POV character. Both are recorded as plan findings (PLAN-DLG-01, PLAN-PARTNER-01) and normalizations; scene_redraft_below re-drafts a scene that came back far below the band once. Absent: the plan is drafted as planned.

scene_redraft_below.description: A drafted scene that has someone beside its POV character on stage and whose measured dialogue-and-속마음 share is below this is re-drafted once, the writer told the measured share and the target; the redraft is kept only when its share is higher (counted as dialogue_redraft). Absent: no redraft.

scene_redraft_ratio.description: ADR-0086 (G5-2): a drafted scene with a partner on stage whose measured talk share is below this fraction of its planned dialogue_density_target is re-drafted once (the redraft is kept only when it talks more). Applies beside scene_redraft_below; absent: only the absolute floor.

partner_in_contract.description: ADR-0086 (G5-2): the chapter contract must put someone other than the POV character on page. A contract without one is sent back to the chapter planner once with that finding; a second miss is recorded as PLAN-PARTNER-02 and the chapter proceeds.

strip_talk_bans.description: ADR-0086 (G5-2): scene must_not lines that forbid talking (e.g. no talk during a fight) are removed from scene plans, recorded as PLAN-DLG-02.

line_targets.description: ADR-0086 (G5-2): the writer is given countable targets instead of a share: quoted dialogue lines per 1,000자 (median and minimum, the operator's p50 and p10) scaled by the scene's planned share against the operator's median share, and a ceiling of 속마음 lines per 1,000자 (the operator's p90).

identity.description: Identity choices a policy makes for projects composed under it (ADR-0073). Absent: a Korean project composes the newest Korean language layer up to lang/ko@5, as before.

language_layer.description: The language layer a new project composes, e.g. lang/ko@6. Used only for projects whose manuscript language matches.

device_lexicon.description: ADR-0084 (U2, live defect G-1): a new project records its premise device from the intake (regression, reincarnation, game or novel possession); writers, editors, planners and the genre judge get that device's vocabulary, and every evaluated version is checked for the other devices' words (KO-DEVICE-01, a major genre finding). Absent or false: the genre overlay's vocabulary alone, as before.

voice_profile.description: ADR-0083 (C3): the operator voice profile (examples/voice-profiles) a new project in the profile's language copies into its composed identity. Absent: no operator voice section.

operator_exemplars.description: ADR-0083 (C5): at novel start a new project pins per_function passages of each listed scene function from corpus.passages (tagger), preferring chapters in the project's point of view; they replace the studio's synthetic exemplars. A database without passages pins none. Absent: studio exemplars only.

prompts.description: The newest prompt family version this policy's jobs may pin (ADR-0081): the job's prompt set is the newest active version per family at or below max_version. Absent: 4.5.0, the newest version when the field was introduced, so earlier policies keep their prompts when a new version is added.

provider_retry.description: Retry and backoff for retryable provider failures (ADR-0072): HTTP 429 and 5xx (502/503/504 included), transport faults and, when retry_empty_reply is true, an empty completion. After each such failure the gateway waits base_delay_ms × multiplier^(n−1), capped at max_delay_ms (with full jitter a uniform share of it), moves to the class's next route and wraps to the first, up to max_attempts provider attempts per call. Every attempt and its backoff is recorded on the call's audit row. Absent: the next route at once, at most four attempts, as before.

refusal.description: A declined request (ADR-0080): a content_filter or safety finish, a safety block in an error body, or (detect_text) a short reply that is a refusal instead of the requested output. The same request is sent again on the same route at most max_retries times, then the call fails MODEL_REFUSED. The request is never softened. Absent: refusals are counted and recorded and the call proceeds as before.

early_stop_margin_points.description: Stop generating further candidates when an auto-approvable candidate exceeds EVERY gated dimension's threshold by at least this margin (per dimension; never an aggregate)

tie_fallback_ladder_authorized.description: Authorizes the deterministic ADR-0015 tie ladder (higher gated-dimension total → fewer patches → lower candidate slot) to decide a pair the position-swapped comparator could not separate. When false, an unresolved pair ends the selection in needs_attention instead of being decided by a fallback. This is the ONLY authorization for the ladder; no other policy field may be read as implying it.

selection_schedule.description: How N candidates are reduced to one. stable_slot_single_elimination: candidates are ordered by their stable slot and reduced by sequential single elimination. The outcome is deterministic FOR THIS PINNED SCHEDULE and the schedule is persisted as provenance; it is not a claim of schedule-independent global optimality, because the pairwise comparator is not guaranteed transitive (ADR-0015).

gates.description: Per-dimension acceptance. auto_approvable = all deterministic criteria pass AND blocking_count = 0 AND major_count = 0 AND every listed dimension score >= its threshold. No aggregate score is ever used.

minor_below.description: Model issues below this confidence are capped at minor

drift_flag_scene_repair_ratio.description: Share of paragraphs flagged for one drift class (at judge confidence >= drift_flag_min_confidence) that triggers a scene-level repair plan instead of per-paragraph patches

chapter_regenerate_ratio.description: Share of flagged paragraphs above which the chapter is regenerated

previous_tail_words.description: Verbatim tail of the previous accepted chapter (sentence-aligned)

previous_tail_floor_words.description: Lowest the degradation ladder may shrink the tail to

previous_tail_extend_to_scene_below_word.description: Extend the tail backward to the start of the last scene when that scene is shorter than this

story_memory.description: ADR-0076: hierarchical story memory. With arc_summaries, when a chapter's arc starts, every earlier scheduled arc whose chapters are all accepted gets one arc summary (L2) from its accepted L1 summaries (the arc_summarizer role, at most l2_max_chars), and the story-so-far section gives the writer, the chapter planner and the continuity checker the L1 summaries of the last recent_chapters accepted chapters in blocks of ten and one L2 item for each older arc. Absent: the story so far is every L1 summary in blocks of ten (ADR-0061).

input_budget_tokens.description: Input token budget per pack template other than the writer (which uses writer_input_budget_tokens); keys are template names such as pack.chapter_planner

passes.description: Independent extractor passes (2 = A and B)

single_source_min_confidence.description: Only-in-one-pass items at or above this confidence with verifiable evidence are accepted as single_source; below → adjudicate

fuzzy_anchor_min_ratio.description: Evidence quotes not found exactly may be re-anchored when similarity >= this ratio; else the item is rejected

scene_calibration.description: ADR-0075 (K3): the length a scene writer is asked for. The scene plan keeps its target; the writer is asked for request_ratio × the target, and with redistribute the targets of the remaining scenes are rescaled by the chapter's remaining budget (the planned total minus what the earlier scenes measured), clamped to [min_ratio, max_ratio]. Evaluation still measures the chapter against the contract's target. Absent: the writer is asked for the plan's target.

override_matrix.description: issue kind → override class (ADR-0042). Kinds not listed default to `reviewer` for major and `advisory` for minor/note.

project_escalations.description: Project-level raises (kind → class); may only raise, never lower

judge_weight.description: Share of the dimension score from the judge; the remainder comes from the deterministic composite (lint / register / terminology)
